clue.text: Real Madrid, turning out, display a butterfly

indicators.note: turning out suggests the football club's name is being reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: The Spanish football team takes the field in a showy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges REALMADRID into the answer; 'display' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A red admiral is a common European butterfly with red-banded black wings.

definitions.meaning: rotten here means foul-smelling or putrid
a row is a line, as in a taxi line or a line of soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a riding track in London's Hyde Park; split it into two words and each defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means foul-smelling, and also a line of people or things standing side by side.

clue.text: Girl goes to Reading for amusement…

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
a reading is an interpretation or version of something

explanation.surface: A young woman travels to the Berkshire town of Reading to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the English town (capital R from its position), but it means an interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a pastime or entertainment that takes one's mind off things.

clue.text: English lady to set up stall

indicators.note: set up here means arranged afresh, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An Englishwoman is about to erect a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' rearranges E plus LADY; 'stall' is a verb, meaning to put off.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time, putting something off.

definitions.meaning: to turn the corner is to pass the critical point and start getting better
to rally is to recover strength after illness or setback

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a motor rally driver taking a bend; both phrases instead mean getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better, as a patient recovering, fits both turning the corner and rallying.

definitions.meaning: someone who assists or encourages another
split as two words, a better is one superior to another

explanation.definitionFit: An abettor assists another, and split in two the word reads as one who is superior.

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: scant means barely sufficient

explanation.surface: Reading something with very little attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of SCANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a document is to examine it closely, so it is a synonym of studying.

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP gaining promotion in the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a party member but means an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, which is to go up.

clue.text: Intense rivalry over job of felling, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a needle match is one of intense rivalry, so needle means bitter rivalry
work is a job

explanation.surface: Bitter rivalry between lumberjacks over who cuts down trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Felling here is a sewing term (a felled seam), not cutting down trees, which is why it is marked 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Felling is a technique of sewing a seam flat, an example of stitching craft.

clue.text: One usually has a second helping

definitions.text: One usually has a second helping

parts.words: One usually has a second helping
parts.note: the surface suggests a greedy diner, but the second is the assistant in a formal fight with pistols or swords

explanation.definitionFit: A participant in a formal fight with swords or pistols traditionally had a second to assist.

clue.text: Romance of wild love after midday

indicators.note: after means the rearranged word follows the midday letter

parts.note: N is the middle letter of the word day, its mid point

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters are scattered out of order

explanation.surface: A passionate love affair beginning after lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges LOVE to OVEL, placed after N, the middle letter of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a long fictional story, a book-length narrative.

clue.text: Bias of 10 perhaps, as concomitant of pride

definitions.meaning: a bias is a preconceived partiality

definitions.text: of 10 perhaps, as concomitant of pride
definitions.meaning: 10 is the answer to 10 Across, a book; Jane Austen's work pairs this with Pride in its title

explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's book Pride and Prejudice supplies the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is a preconceived bias, and Austen's novel couples it with pride.

clue.text: Cargo yet to be placed for Confederate soldier?

indicators.note: to be placed suggests the letters still need to be put in their new positions

explanation.surface: A shipment waiting to be stowed for a Southern soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be placed' rearranges CARGOYET.
explanation.definitionFit: Confederate troops in the American Civil War wore grey uniforms, so a grey-coated soldier is one of them.

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A political party registering a Spanish brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB is the UK Labour Party, one of Britain's main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a brand name or trade name under which goods are sold.

parts.note: having the wind up is British slang for being scared; scared when up high is the reading

explanation.walkthrough: 'The wind up' is British slang for fear; add 'up' and it is fear of heights.
explanation.definitionFit: This phobia is the fear of heights, so being frightened when up high.

definitions.meaning: a newly invented word or phrase
all the coins, or small change, of a currency taken together

explanation.walkthrough: 'All change' is what a British train guard calls at the end of the line; here it means all the coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A new word is a coinage, and the coins of a currency collectively are its coinage.

parts.note: Macbeth speaks of vaulting ..., the drive that brings about his end

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Macbeth he admits he has only 'vaulting ambition, which o'erleaps itself'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth's overreaching drive for power, described as vaulting, leads to his downfall.

clue.text: A brown I mixed from lots of other colours

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist mixes brown from a palette of other colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges ABROWNI; the surface suggests paint mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow shows a band of many colours, red through violet.

parts.note: a bar is the counter in a pub
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: A rival bid put forward by a member of pub staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter-offer' reads as one business term but splits into its two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks behind the bar, an employee of a pub.

definitions.meaning: a single volume reprinting several works
a bus, from the old full name of the vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus edition gathers several works in one volume, and the word was the original name for a bus.

clue.text: This Armstrong rested, with companion, on near side of moon

indicators.note: on means the following piece comes after, attached to the previous ones

parts.note: sat means rested
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: the near side is the first half of the word moon

explanation.surface: A moon-walking astronaut resting with a partner on the lunar surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Neil Armstrong on the moon, but the answer is the jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong's nickname; 'near side of' takes the first half of MOON, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the nickname of Louis Armstrong, the jazz trumpeter.

clue.text: Pander to sovereign as provider of food

parts.note: to cater to someone is to pander to them
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Indulging the monarch's tastes as the royal cook.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for functions.

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: bliss is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Choosing between wine or a cuppa, both endlessly delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last S from BLISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white French wine from Burgundy.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for army

parts.note: a host is an army or multitude

explanation.surface: A musician serving for years in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets suite.

parts.note: a lot means many
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A flower whose influence gives rise to many nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is an aquatic plant of the water lily kind.

clue.text: Royal Navy faster, perhaps, to hand over

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A naval vessel going quicker to deliver something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RN plus FASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to convey or pass something to another person.

definitions.meaning: to drudge is to toil, as when cleaning hard
an unimportant, stunted person, a nobody

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to toil at hard cleaning, and a scrub is also an insignificant, inferior person.

definitions.meaning: a flare fired from a pistol, named after its American inventor

explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare fired from a pistol, named after Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely is the adverb sense, and a Very light is a coloured signal flare.

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone awry and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A marriage commitment postponed, with both parties calling it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LATERBOTH; the bracket makes it look like a jilting.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a formal promise to marry.

clue.text: High-pressure area, torrid generally in the interior

indicators.note: in the interior means the letters lie inside the run of words torrid generally

explanation.surface: A weather report: a hot inland region under high pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'torRID GEnerally'.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology a ridge is an elongated region of high atmospheric pressure.

indicators.note: cooking implies the letters are stirred up and transformed

explanation.surface: A kitchen alcove for preparing vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges PEAS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted semicircular recess in a church.

clue.text: Unwanted third party is often a fool

definitions.meaning: someone who tags along with a couple wanting to be alone
a fool is a creamy fruit dessert, commonly made with this green berry

explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit and cream; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tagalong with a couple is called this in British slang, and the green fruit is often made into a fool pudding.
